article.title: have got frente a have
article.part: Registro, variación y norma — Register, variation, and standard usage
article.chapter: Variedades del inglés — Varieties of English

claims.summary: English possessive have and have got can both describe present possession and states (I have a car / I've got a car), with have got especially common in informal British English while plain have is more general. Ordinary lexical have commonly uses do-support in questions (Do you have ...?), whereas possessive have got permits auxiliary have (Have you got ...?). Have got in this possessive sense does not generally replace eventive have, as in have breakfast.

links.notes: Reference scope: possessive have/have got, auxiliary distribution and regional register usage.
